{"reconstruction": "CONTEXT. The previous page maps the ellipsoid conformally onto a sphere. Notation: phi is geodetic latitude, psi is the conformal latitude on the sphere, and e^2 = 619/96100 (flattening 1/310). The map is tan(45+psi/2) = tan(45+phi/2)*((1-e sin phi)/(1+e sin phi))^(e/2)*C. The constant is chosen so that psi = P on the central parallel. The sphere radius is r = a/sqrt(1-e^2 sin^2 P). This page adds the second step: an oblique stereographic projection of that sphere onto the plane tangent at the point (latitude P, longitude 0). The result is a conformal 'double stereographic' projection.

CONVENTIONS (deduced from the examples). The origin is the central point. x is positive to the SOUTH along the central meridian. y is positive to the WEST. The plane scale is 2r, so a point at angular distance c from the centre lies at 2r tan(c/2).

1. INVERSE MAPPING BY BIPOLAR COORDINATES (plane to sphere).
- The north pole images at x = -2r tan(45-P/2); the south pole at x = +2r tan(45+P/2).
- Gauss sets 2r tan(45-P/2) + x = A cos(alpha), y = A sin(alpha). So A and alpha are the distance and direction of the point seen from the image of N.
- He sets 2r tan(45+P/2) - x = B cos(C), y = B sin(C). So B and C are the same seen from the image of S.
- Meridians are circles through N' and S'. By the tangent-chord / inscribed-angle theorem, longitude = alpha + C.
- Parallels are Apollonius circles with A/B constant. This gives tan(45+psi/2) = B tan(45-P/2)/A. The check at the origin gives psi = P; A = 0 gives 90 deg; B = 0 gives -90 deg.
- The meridian direction at the point makes the angle alpha - C with the x-axis; this is the meridian convergence.
- The parallel through the point cuts the axis orthogonally at x0 = 2r tan((P-psi)/2). The chord from the point to x0 bisects the tangent rotation. Hence x + y tan((alpha-C)/2) = 2r tan((P-psi)/2).
- All of this is correct.

2. CONSTANTS.
- Quadrant of the equator = 10^7 m * (1 + e^2/4 + 7e^4/64 + 15e^6/256). This is the reciprocal of the meridian-quadrant series 1 - e^2/4 - 3e^4/64 - 5e^6/256, with the meridian quadrant = 10^7 m by the metre definition.

- Pole images: 2r tan(45-P/2) = 2829198 and 2r tan(45+P/2) = 15178752 toises. All of these verify.
